"""Turns a run's check results into its score. Called by harness/run.py."""


def compose_score(checks, pass_mark):
    total = sum(c.weight for c in checks)
    earned = sum(c.weight for c in checks if c.passed)
    score = earned / total if total else 0.0
    gates_ok = all(c.passed for c in checks if c.gate)
    return {
        "score": round(score, 4),
        "passed": gates_ok and score >= pass_mark,
        "gates_ok": gates_ok,
        "checks": [c.to_json() for c in checks],
    }

def score_run(checks, pass_mark):

priorTurns.text: Also, is lead-free solder harder to work with?

Yes, somewhat harder, for three reasons:

- **Higher melting point.** Common lead-free solder (SAC305: tin, 3% silver, 0.5% copper) melts at about 217 to 220 °C. Classic tin-lead (63/37) melts at 183 °C. You need a hotter iron, roughly 350 °C instead of 315 °C. In reflow, peak temperature rises from about 215 to 225 °C to about 240 to 250 °C. Components and boards tolerate a limited peak, so the safe window between "melted properly" and "damaged" gets narrower.
- **Worse wetting.** Lead-free solder has higher surface tension, so it spreads more slowly and reluctantly. It also leans harder on flux to clean the surface.
- **Looks different.** Lead-free joints often cool dull and grainy, where tin-lead goes shiny. A dull joint isn't necessarily bad. Judge it by its shape (a smooth concave fillet), not by shine.

Tin-lead also has a practical advantage: 63/37 is a eutectic, meaning it goes straight from solid to liquid at one temperature, with no mushy in-between stage. Joints set instantly, so small movements while cooling matter less.

Lead-free is the default for anything you sell or plan to use long-term because of regulations like RoHS (the EU rule restricting lead). For personal learning, leaded solder is easier, but wash your hands afterward and don't eat while soldering.

# Scoring (GRD-2)

- Each check has a class: dead (the board does not work), degraded (works, but worse), cosmetic (looks only).
- Q: their weighted average, with cosmetic checks counting a tenth.
- The worst failed class picks the band; Q places the reward inside it.

"""GRD-2 scoring: turns a board's check results into its reward. Called by harness/run.py."""

CLASS_WEIGHT = {"dead": 1.0, "degraded": 1.0, "cosmetic": 0.1}
PASS_MARK = 0.5  # same for every task


def compose_scores(board, items):
    """items: (class, score 0..1, failed) per check."""
    if board is None:
        return 0.0  # no board handed in at all
    num = sum(CLASS_WEIGHT[c] * s for c, s, _ in items)
    den = sum(CLASS_WEIGHT[c] for c, _, _ in items)
    q = num / den if den else 0.0
    failed = {c for c, _, f in items if f}
    if "dead" in failed:
        return 0.01 + 0.24 * q
    if "degraded" in failed:
        return 0.25 + 0.25 * q
    return 0.50 + 0.50 * q  # only cosmetic checks failed, or none

input.reply:
**What the scores are.** The model's last layer outputs one raw number per token in its vocabulary. These numbers are called **logits**.

**How they become a choice.** The **softmax** function converts logits into probabilities:

$$p_i = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_j e^{z_j}}$$

# tiny-dllm

A small, readable serving engine for **diffusion language models**, the way vLLM serves
autoregressive ones: paged KV cache, prefix caching, step-level continuous batching, and an
OpenAI-compatible HTTP server. About 1,200 lines of Python, CPU only.

It runs [`dllm-hub/Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1`](https://huggingface.co/dllm-hub/Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1)
(Apache-2.0): Qwen3-0.6B fine-tuned with [dLLM](https://github.com/ZHZisZZ/dllm) into a
**block diffusion** model (BD3LM). Instead of writing one token at a time, it writes the answer
in blocks of 32 tokens: each block starts as 32 `<|mask|>` tokens and is filled in over several
denoising steps, in whatever order the model is most sure about.


## Benchmark

8-core desktop CPU, fp32, greedy, block 32, threshold 0.9, up to 128 answer tokens,
best of 3 (the machine was also running other work). The **reference loop** is the plain block
diffusion loop: one request at a time, no KV cache, the whole sequence recomputed every denoising
step. Every mode produced exactly the same tokens (checked by the benchmark).

| mode                                     |   time | tokens | forward passes | committed / step | tok/s | speedup |
| ---------------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | -------------: | ---------------: | ----: | ------: |
| reference loop, 1 request                | 11.75s |     78 |             90 |             1.16 |   6.6 |    1.0x |
| engine, 1 request                        |  6.82s |     78 |             90 |             1.16 |  11.4 |    1.7x |
| reference loop, 8 requests one at a time | 73.28s |    538 |            572 |             1.22 |   7.3 |    1.0x |
| engine, 8 concurrent requests            | 25.94s |    538 |             99 |             1.22 |  20.7 |    2.8x |

"Committed / step" counts every slot unmasked in a step, including the end-of-text padding the
model fills in after the answer. At threshold 0.9 this 0.6B model is rarely sure of more than one
token at a time; lower the threshold for more parallelism (0.5 gives about 1.6, slightly different
text). On a CPU a single 32-token block already keeps the cores fairly busy (a forward pass costs
about 2.6 ms per token for one block and 1.6 ms per token for a 256-token batch), so batching
gains less than it would on a GPU; most of the single-request speedup is the KV cache.

"""Benchmark on this machine (CPU, fp32, Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1), greedy, threshold 0.9.

Compares the plain block-diffusion loop (reference.py: one request at a time, no KV cache, the
whole sequence recomputed every denoising step) with the engine (paged KV cache, step-level
batching), for 1 request and for N concurrent requests. Every mode produces exactly the same
tokens, which is checked, so tokens/s compare the same work. Each timing is the best of --repeats. On a hybrid CPU, pin to the performance cores:

    taskset -c 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14 python bench.py [--num-requests 8] [--max-tokens 128] [--repeats 2]
"""

import argparse
import time

import torch

from tiny_dllm import Engine, EngineConfig, SamplingParams
from tiny_dllm.model import Qwen3
from tiny_dllm.reference import reference_generate

QUESTIONS = [
    "Explain in a short paragraph why the sky is blue.",
    "Describe how a bicycle stays upright, in a few sentences.",
    "Write a short paragraph about the history of the printing press.",
    "Explain what a hash function is to a beginner.",
    "Give three tips for writing clear documentation, with one sentence each.",
    "Describe the water cycle in a short paragraph.",
    "Explain why the moon has phases.",
    "Summarize what photosynthesis does, in a few sentences.",
]


def run_engine(engine: Engine, prompts, params) -> tuple[float, list, int]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    reqs = [engine.add_request(p, params) for p in prompts]
    while engine.has_unfinished():
        engine.step()
    return time.perf_counter() - start, reqs, engine.num_steps


def run_reference(model, prompts, params, config, mask_id) -> tuple[float, list, int]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    reqs = [reference_generate(model, p, params, config.block_size, config.threshold, mask_id) for p in prompts]
    return time.perf_counter() - start, reqs, sum(r.num_steps for r in reqs)  # one forward pass per step


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--num-requests", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--threads", type=int, default=8)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    n, r = args.num_requests, args.repeats

    config = EngineConfig(num_threads=args.threads, max_num_seqs=max(n, 1))
    model = Qwen3.from_pretrained(config.model)
    engine = Engine(config, model=model)
    tok = engine.tokenizer
    prompts = [tok.encode(tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": QUESTIONS[i % len(QUESTIONS)]}])) for i in range(n)]
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=args.max_tokens)
    run_engine(engine, prompts[:2], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8))  # warm up

    def fresh_engine():  # a new engine per run: no prefix-cache hits from the previous run
        return Engine(config, model=model, tokenizer=tok)

    modes = [
        ("reference loop, 1 request", lambda: run_reference(model, prompts[:1], params, config, tok.mask_id)),
        ("engine, 1 request", lambda: run_engine(fresh_engine(), prompts[:1], params)),
        (f"reference loop, {n} requests one at a time", lambda: run_reference(model, prompts, params, config, tok.mask_id)),
        (f"engine, {n} concurrent requests", lambda: run_engine(fresh_engine(), prompts, params)),
    ]
    rows, outputs = [], {}
    for name, fn in modes:
        best, reqs, forwards = min((fn() for _ in range(r)), key=lambda x: x[0])
        tokens = sum(len(q.output_ids) for q in reqs)
        committed_per_step = sum(q.num_committed for q in reqs) / sum(q.num_steps for q in reqs)
        rows.append((name, best, tokens, forwards, committed_per_step))
        outputs[name] = [q.output_ids for q in reqs]
        print(f"  done: {name} ({best:.1f}s)", flush=True)

    same = outputs[modes[0][0]] == outputs[modes[1][0]] and outputs[modes[2][0]] == outputs[modes[3][0]]
    print(f"\nQwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1, fp32, CPU ({torch.get_num_threads()} threads), best of {r} runs")
    print(f"block size {config.block_size}, confidence threshold {config.threshold}, greedy, max_tokens {args.max_tokens}")
    print(f"identical tokens in every mode: {'yes' if same else 'NO'}\n")
    print(f"  {'mode':<44}{'time':>8}{'tokens':>8}{'forwards':>10}{'commit/step':>13}{'tok/s':>8}{'speedup':>9}")
    for i, (name, secs, tokens, forwards, cps) in enumerate(rows):
        base = rows[0][1] if i < 2 else rows[2][1]
        print(f"  {name:<44}{secs:>7.2f}s{tokens:>8}{forwards:>10}{cps:>13.2f}{tokens / secs:>8.1f}{base / secs:>8.1f}x")
    print("\n  tokens: answer tokens, up to end of text. forwards: model forward passes (the engine runs one")
    print("  batched pass per step for every running request). commit/step: slots unmasked per denoising")
    print("  step per request, including the end-of-text padding the model fills in after the answer.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# tiny-dllm

A small, readable serving engine for **diffusion language models**, the way vLLM serves
autoregressive ones: paged KV cache, prefix caching, step-level continuous batching, and an
OpenAI-compatible HTTP server. About 1,200 lines of Python, CPU only.

It runs [`dllm-hub/Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1`](https://huggingface.co/dllm-hub/Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1)
(Apache-2.0): Qwen3-0.6B fine-tuned with [dLLM](https://github.com/ZHZisZZ/dllm) into a
**block diffusion** model (BD3LM). Instead of writing one token at a time, it writes the answer
in blocks of 32 tokens: each block starts as 32 `<|mask|>` tokens and is filled in over several
denoising steps, in whatever order the model is most sure about.


## Benchmark

8-core desktop CPU, fp32, greedy, block 32, threshold 0.9, up to 128 answer tokens,
best of 3 (the machine was also running other work). The **reference loop** is the plain block
diffusion loop: one request at a time, no KV cache, the whole sequence recomputed every denoising
step. Every mode produced exactly the same tokens (checked by the benchmark).

| mode                                     |   time | tokens | forward passes | committed / step | tok/s | speedup |
| ---------------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | -------------: | ---------------: | ----: | ------: |
| reference loop, 1 request                | 11.75s |     78 |             90 |             1.16 |   6.6 |    1.0x |
| engine, 1 request                        |  6.82s |     78 |             90 |             1.16 |  11.4 |    1.7x |
| reference loop, 8 requests one at a time | 73.28s |    538 |            572 |             1.22 |   7.3 |    1.0x |
| engine, 8 concurrent requests            | 25.94s |    538 |             99 |             1.22 |  20.7 |    2.8x |

"Committed / step" counts every slot unmasked in a step, including the end-of-text padding the
model fills in after the answer. At threshold 0.9 this 0.6B model is rarely sure of more than one
token at a time; lower the threshold for more parallelism (0.5 gives about 1.6, slightly different
text). On a CPU a single 32-token block already keeps the cores fairly busy (a forward pass costs
about 2.6 ms per token for one block and 1.6 ms per token for a 256-token batch), so batching
gains less than it would on a GPU; most of the single-request speedup is the KV cache.

"""Benchmark on this machine (CPU, fp32, Qwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1), greedy, threshold 0.9.

Compares the plain block-diffusion loop (reference.py: one request at a time, no KV cache, the
whole sequence recomputed every denoising step) with the engine (paged KV cache, step-level
batching), for 1 request and for N concurrent requests. Every mode produces exactly the same
tokens, which is checked, so tokens/s compare the same work. Each timing is the best of --repeats. On a hybrid CPU, pin to the performance cores:

    taskset -c 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14 python bench.py [--num-requests 8] [--max-tokens 128] [--repeats 2]
"""

import argparse
import time

import torch

from tiny_dllm import Engine, EngineConfig, SamplingParams
from tiny_dllm.model import Qwen3
from tiny_dllm.reference import reference_generate

QUESTIONS = [
    "Explain in a short paragraph why the sky is blue.",
    "Describe how a bicycle stays upright, in a few sentences.",
    "Write a short paragraph about the history of the printing press.",
    "Explain what a hash function is to a beginner.",
    "Give three tips for writing clear documentation, with one sentence each.",
    "Describe the water cycle in a short paragraph.",
    "Explain why the moon has phases.",
    "Summarize what photosynthesis does, in a few sentences.",
]


def run_engine(engine: Engine, prompts, params) -> tuple[float, list, int]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    reqs = [engine.add_request(p, params) for p in prompts]
    while engine.has_unfinished():
        engine.step()
    return time.perf_counter() - start, reqs, engine.num_steps


def run_reference(model, prompts, params, config, mask_id) -> tuple[float, list, int]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    reqs = [reference_generate(model, p, params, config.block_size, config.threshold, mask_id) for p in prompts]
    return time.perf_counter() - start, reqs, sum(r.num_steps for r in reqs)  # one forward pass per step


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--num-requests", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--threads", type=int, default=8)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    n, r = args.num_requests, args.repeats

    config = EngineConfig(num_threads=args.threads, max_num_seqs=max(n, 1))
    model = Qwen3.from_pretrained(config.model)
    engine = Engine(config, model=model)
    tok = engine.tokenizer
    prompts = [tok.encode(tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": QUESTIONS[i % len(QUESTIONS)]}])) for i in range(n)]
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=args.max_tokens)
    run_engine(engine, prompts[:2], SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8))  # warm up

    def fresh_engine():  # a new engine per run: no prefix-cache hits from the previous run
        return Engine(config, model=model, tokenizer=tok)

    modes = [
        ("reference loop, 1 request", lambda: run_reference(model, prompts[:1], params, config, tok.mask_id)),
        ("engine, 1 request", lambda: run_engine(fresh_engine(), prompts[:1], params)),
        (f"reference loop, {n} requests one at a time", lambda: run_reference(model, prompts, params, config, tok.mask_id)),
        (f"engine, {n} concurrent requests", lambda: run_engine(fresh_engine(), prompts, params)),
    ]
    rows, outputs = [], {}
    for name, fn in modes:
        best, reqs, forwards = min((fn() for _ in range(r)), key=lambda x: x[0])
        tokens = sum(len(q.output_ids) for q in reqs)
        committed_per_step = sum(q.num_committed for q in reqs) / sum(q.num_steps for q in reqs)
        rows.append((name, best, tokens, forwards, committed_per_step))
        outputs[name] = [q.output_ids for q in reqs]
        print(f"  done: {name} ({best:.1f}s)", flush=True)

    same = outputs[modes[0][0]] == outputs[modes[1][0]] and outputs[modes[2][0]] == outputs[modes[3][0]]
    print(f"\nQwen3-0.6B-diffusion-bd3lm-v0.1, fp32, CPU ({torch.get_num_threads()} threads), best of {r} runs")
    print(f"block size {config.block_size}, confidence threshold {config.threshold}, greedy, max_tokens {args.max_tokens}")
    print(f"identical tokens in every mode: {'yes' if same else 'NO'}\n")
    print(f"  {'mode':<44}{'time':>8}{'tokens':>8}{'forwards':>10}{'commit/step':>13}{'tok/s':>8}{'speedup':>9}")
    for i, (name, secs, tokens, forwards, cps) in enumerate(rows):
        base = rows[0][1] if i < 2 else rows[2][1]
        print(f"  {name:<44}{secs:>7.2f}s{tokens:>8}{forwards:>10}{cps:>13.2f}{tokens / secs:>8.1f}{base / secs:>8.1f}x")
    print("\n  tokens: answer tokens, up to end of text. forwards: model forward passes (the engine runs one")
    print("  batched pass per step for every running request). commit/step: slots unmasked per denoising")
    print("  step per request, including the end-of-text padding the model fills in after the answer.\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
